title: Large Language Models as Data Preprocessors

model.params_source: paper Sec. 4.1 (temperature 0.35; 10 few-shot examples; random batching with batch size 5-10 for GPT-4o); max_tokens assumed

task.subset_rule: all (Restaurant data-imputation test split of the Narayan et al. fm_data_tasks release; 86 rows expected, verify on download)
task.approximation: The 10 few-shot demonstrations with reasons are hand-written by us (the paper's are unlisted); batch composition is a seeded random draw with batch size 7 (paper: 5-10); the exact GPT-4o 'best setting' behind Table 1 is not identified.

items.source: https://fm-data-tasks.s3.us-west-1.amazonaws.com/datasets.tar.gz (HazyResearch/fm_data_tasks release), file data_imputation/Restaurant/test.csv; train.csv for demonstrations
items.license: Apache-2.0 (fm_data_tasks repository); underlying Restaurant dataset license not stated

placeholders.few_shot_block:
10 demonstrations in the Sec. 3.2 layout: 'Users:
Question 1: Record is [Data Instance 1]. What is the city?
...
Assistant:
Answer 1: [Reason 1]
[Answer 1]
...' where each data instance is contextualized as [name: "...", addr: "...", phone: "...", type: "...", city: ???] (Sec. 3.3) and each reason follows the printed example ('The phone number "770" suggests that the city should be either Atlanta or Marietta in Georgia. The addr attribute suggests a place in Marietta.')
placeholders.batch_questions: one line per test record in the batch: 'Question k: Record is [name: "...", addr: "...", phone: "...", type: "...", city: ???]. What is the city?' (Sec. 3.5 random batching, 5-10 records per call)

prompt.few_shot: k=10 hand-written demonstrations (paper: manually selected and labelled with reasons; not printed)
prompt.source_location: Sec. 3 (template), 3.1 (zero-shot DI prompt), 3.2 (few-shot layout and example reason), 3.3 (contextualization), 3.5 (batch prompting), 4.1 (settings)
prompt.verbatim: partial (role line, zero-shot DI instructions and the few-shot/batch layout are copied verbatim; the 10 demonstrations and their reasons are not printed and are assembled by us)

output.parse: regex ^Answer (\d+):\s*(?P<reason>.*)\n(?P<value>.*)$ per numbered answer; the second line is the imputed city
output.postprocess: strip, lowercase, remove trailing punctuation; missing answer counted as wrong

metric.name: accuracy
metric.definition: fraction of test records whose imputed city equals the gold city after lowercasing and stripping (Narayan et al. DI accuracy convention).
metric.original_location: Table 1, row GPT-4o, column Restaurant (Data Imputation, accuracy %)

open_points: Data download needs a human: the fm_data_tasks archive https://fm-data-tasks.s3.us-west-1.amazonaws.com/datasets.tar.gz is 111 MB (over the 100 MB hook limit) and the Restaurant split has no other public copy (the HazyResearch/fm_data_tasks repository holds code only). Extract data_imputation/Restaurant/train.csv and test.csv to halflife/external/data/tierb_items/fm_data_tasks/; a hook can then build the batched few-shot prompts (10 seeded train rows with a fixed reason template following the printed example, batches of 7) and parse the two-line answers.
Demonstration reasons: accept 10 seeded train rows with a fixed reason template (the paper's hand-written reasons are not printed).
notes: Set-level comparison only: the paper's n is not printed. Batching is done with 7 records per call (13 calls per seed). The data-type hint sentence of Sec. 3.1 is not used for the 'city' attribute. || [hooks_2 2026-09-07] reviewed for a per-paper hook: archive over the 100 MB download limit; no hook written.
hook: none (needs_human: archive over the 100 MB download limit)
